h1: Brighton Hotel Bangkok — bright modern rooms a 10-minute walk from BITEC, with an indoor pool
intro: If you want a 3-star hotel in Bang Na that goes beyond a clean bed and a desk — somewhere with a pool, a gym, a restaurant, a spa, free parking and a complimentary shuttle to the convention centre — Brighton Hotel Bangkok is one of the most frequently mentioned names in the neighbourhood. Sitting at 222 Sanphawut Road in Bang Na district, the hotel is around 800 m from Bangkok International Trade and Exhibition Centre (BITEC): a comfortable 10-minute walk, with a free hotel shuttle available during exhibition periods. All 162 rooms are styled with floor-to-ceiling windows and private balconies that fill each room with natural light. It scores 8.4 from 278 real guest reviews on Trip.com, with service rated at 8.8. Rooms start from approximately ฿1,350/night in the low season, rising to ฿2,200–2,500 during major BITEC events.

body.html: Brighton Hotel Bangkok positions itself as a mid-range 3-star property that caters to both business travellers attending BITEC exhibitions and leisure guests wanting a comfortable base in the Bang Na corridor. Sanphawut Road, where the hotel stands, is a main artery running from Bang Na toward Sukhumvit. BITEC — Bangkok International Trade and Exhibition Centre — is under 1 km away, a relaxed 10-minute walk, and the hotel runs a complimentary shuttle to BITEC during exhibition periods, which is why trade-show and Expo attendees frequently put it on the shortlist.

The 162 rooms range from 38 sqm (Deluxe) to 72 sqm (Junior Suite and Executive Two Bedroom Suite). The single most consistent praise across real reviews is the large windows — floor-to-ceiling glass that floods each room with natural daylight and makes the space feel more open than the square footage alone suggests. Every room comes with a private balcony, free Wi-Fi, an in-room safe, a flat-screen TV and an en-suite bathroom; some Deluxe rooms have a rain shower, and suites have a bathtub. Furnishings are clean-lined modern in neutral tones — nothing over-designed, but comfortable and well-maintained by the majority of reviewers.
"Bright room, much bigger than I expected for the price. Great location for BITEC — easy walk. Staff was friendly throughout. Will definitely return."

Where Brighton pulls noticeably ahead of budget alternatives in the same strip is its facilities package. There is an indoor swimming pool plus a children's pool, a fitness centre, a spa with Thai massage, a bar and a full-service restaurant. Trip.com reviewers rated service 8.8 and cleanliness 8.5 — both strong figures for a 3-star property. The indoor pool is consistently praised as a genuine bonus at this price point. The one caveat from reviews: on weekend mornings families with young children can make the pool area noisy — if a peaceful swim matters, aim for early weekday mornings. Free parking is included, plus airport transfer services to Suvarnabhumi Airport are available at an additional charge.

The Bang Na neighbourhood gives Brighton a strategic edge that is easily underestimated. BITEC is within walking distance; Mega Bangna — home to Thailand's IKEA — is a 7-minute drive; Central Bangna is under 5 minutes by car; and Bangkok Mall, the recently opened large-format shopping complex billed as the biggest in Southeast Asia, is in the same corridor. Suvarnabhumi Airport is only about 20–25 minutes by road, making the hotel a convenient overnight stay before or after an international flight. BTS Bang Na station is around 15 minutes on foot — not close by Bangkok standards, so guests relying on the Skytrain for all-day sightseeing should factor that in.

A candid look at the reviews reveals a split worth understanding. On Trip.com (8.4/10, 278 reviews) and Booking.com (7.8/10, 467 reviews) the overall tone is positive, with cleanliness and service consistently praised. On TripAdvisor (71 reviews, 3.3/5) a smaller sample flags older air-conditioning units and dust accumulation in some rooms. Street noise from Sanphawut Road appears in reviews for lower-floor front-facing rooms. These are manageable issues — ask for a higher floor or an inner-facing room — but worth knowing before booking. A small number of Booking.com reviews also note occasional Wi-Fi instability in certain rooms.

The overall picture of Brighton Hotel Bangkok is a 3-star property that punches above its category in facilities while keeping rates competitive. If your reason for being in Bang Na is a BITEC event, a shopping run to Mega Bangna or Bangkok Mall, or a pre-flight overnight before Suvarnabhumi — and you want a pool, a gym, a restaurant and free parking without jumping to a 4-star budget — Brighton delivers. The score of 8.4 on Trip.com and 7.8 on Booking.com from a combined 745+ reviews suggests the majority of guests leave satisfied.

A few practical tips picked up from tracking reviews here: book early and compare prices across Agoda, Booking and Trip.com — rates during major BITEC events can jump 50–80% from the standard price. During non-event periods, the gap between platforms can be surprisingly wide. If you are driving, free parking is straightforward on regular days but fills faster when a large exhibition is running — arrive early on those dates or consider coming by BTS if you only need brief access to the venue.

honestSummary: Brighton Hotel Bangkok is a 3-star property that delivers more facility value than its star rating implies. For guests in Bang Na for a BITEC event, a shopping trip to Mega Bangna or Bangkok Mall, or a pre-flight overnight, the combination of an indoor pool, gym, spa, restaurant, free parking and a BITEC shuttle at a competitive rate is hard to beat in this district. The caveats — street noise on lower floors, occasional A/C quirks, a 15-minute walk to BTS — are real but manageable with a little room selection strategy.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Brighton Hotel Bangkok

faq.q: Where is Brighton Hotel Bangkok and how far is it from BITEC?
faq.a: Brighton Hotel Bangkok is at 222 Sanphawut Road, Bang Na Nuea subdistrict, Bang Na district, Bangkok 10260. BITEC Bang Na (Bangkok International Trade and Exhibition Centre) is approximately 800 m away — a 10-minute walk — and the hotel provides a free shuttle to BITEC during exhibition periods. BTS Bang Na station is about 1.2 km away, a 15-minute walk.

faq.q: What is the starting price at Brighton Hotel Bangkok and what room types are available?
faq.a: Rooms start from approximately ฿1,350/night for a Deluxe Room (38 sqm) in the low season. A Junior Suite starts at around ฿2,100, and the Executive Two Bedroom Suite at approx. ฿3,500. Rates rise significantly — sometimes 50–80% — during major BITEC exhibitions, so book early and compare prices across Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com.

faq.q: Does Brighton Hotel Bangkok have a swimming pool and gym?
faq.a: Yes. The hotel has an indoor swimming pool with a separate children's pool, a fitness centre, and a spa with Thai massage services — a notably generous amenities package for a 3-star rate in Bangkok. The pool is praised by reviewers as a genuine bonus at this price point.

faq.q: Who is Brighton Hotel Bangkok best suited for?
faq.a: It is best suited to business travellers attending BITEC exhibitions who want a comfortable hotel within walking distance of the venue, with a pool and gym to unwind after conference days. It also works well for families or couples on leisure trips using Bang Na as a base for Mega Bangna (with IKEA), Bangkok Mall and Suvarnabhumi Airport, which is only 20–25 minutes by car.

faq.q: Is there road noise? How do I get a quieter room?
faq.a: Sanphawut Road is a busy arterial, and some lower-floor front-facing rooms pick up traffic noise during the day and evening. The straightforward fix: request a high-floor or inner-facing room when booking or at check-in. The majority of positive reviews on Trip.com and Booking.com come from guests in mid-to-high-floor rooms.

faq.q: What shopping is near Brighton Hotel Bangkok?
faq.a: Several major retail destinations are within a short drive: Mega Bangna (home to Thailand's IKEA) is about 4 km away (7 min by Grab); Central Bangna is around 3 km; and Bangkok Mall, the recently opened large-format complex positioned as Southeast Asia's largest, is in the same Bang Na corridor, approximately 10 minutes by car. Suvarnabhumi Airport is about 17 km away, or 20–25 minutes by road.
